questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, wear clothes that protect you from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as extreme fatigue can happen when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean in the right direction, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward.

questions.question: How can you discourage another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This makes it harder for car drivers to try to share your space.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when the rider downshifts.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If operating a three-wheeled motorcycle or riding with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right of your lane because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. If you ride too far right, the sidecar may leave the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel could also go off the road if you get too close to the edge.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever with all four fingers. Apply firm pressure, then gradually increase it as needed.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the vehicle in front of you to help see.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther back from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see more of the road. Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Normally, you should maintain a following distance of:
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, leave at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction you want to go. Keep your feet up to avoid catching them on the road. Always watch for other traffic around you.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Sound the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle to use their headlights when riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes slowing down, increasing your distance from other vehicles, using the headlights of cars ahead to see better, using your high beam (unless following or meeting a car), and changing your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: What should a good face shield NOT do?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be clear, let you see to the sides, attach securely, and allow air to pass through. A shield that blocks air causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view and makes oncoming traffic see you better.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see.
Ride only in the left part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam (unless you are following or meeting another car), use other cars' headlights to see, and wear reflective clothes. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe.

questions.question: When a group of motorcycles exits a highway, which formation should they use?
questions.explanation: Use staggered formation for most group riding. Switch to single file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, ride in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, straighten the handlebars, and then stop.
Push both brakes hard while still leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, straighten the handlebars, and then stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop in a curve, straighten up and straighten the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will do so.

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain starts, the road is very slippery because oil from cars has not washed away. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 mph.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: The best protection for a motorcycle rider is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
A good understanding of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best protection against crashes is to keep distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper protective gear is also important.

questions.question: Of crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep while riding?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.
